purpose: Provide a reusable high-skill strategic cognition layer between StoryBox visibility/legal-action state and StoryBox world resolution.

test_evidence.note: The SCK tests are pytest-style functions, not unittest.TestCase classes. 'python -m unittest discover -s tests' collects 0 of them, so HANDOFF.md's unittest command cannot verify this component.

live_runner_environment.install: python -m venv .venv-textarena && .venv-textarena/Scripts/python.exe -m pip install textarena pytest

implemented_capabilities: evidence ledger with reliability-tempered likelihood-ratio updates
generic two-ply expected-value planner across hidden-world hypotheses
live TextArena SecretMafia self-play runner (one policy drives every seat)
actor-view boundary: roles recovered only from the actor's own private prompt
explicit hand-specified behavior evidence model (night kill, doctor save)
static and empirical information-leakage audits for the decision path
native [N] target-action encoding so day-vote evidence survives the observation stream
paired cross-play harness against a frozen baseline with role-assigned arms
vote-coordination mechanism diagnostic (bloc voting vs inference)
deliberately_not_implemented_yet: learned evidence-likelihood model (replay calibration still pending)
nested theory of mind beyond one-step opponent action models

environment_constraints.vote_targets_are_observable_with_the_nat: state.add_observation strips every '[Player N]' role tag from PLAYER_ACTION messages, but the environment's own prompts ask for the '[X]' form and VoteHandler accepts it. The runner submits '[N]', so day-vote targets reach later actors intact. Submitting '[Player N]' reproduces the earlier broken behaviour where votes arrived as the empty string; that form is kept only as a test control. See native_vote_channel for the measured comparison.
observable_evidence_events: Player X was killed during the night.
Player X was eliminated by vote.
Player X IS [NOT] a Mafia member. (Detective, private)
public day votes with their targets intact, because the runner submits the native [N] form
environment_constraints.day_number_never_increments: The environment never advances game_state['day_number'], so the runner keeps its own night counter.
environment_constraints.global_random_seeding: SecretMafiaEnv.reset seeds the global random module. Policies therefore use their own random.Random instance so they cannot perturb environment randomness.
environment_constraints.residual_consequence: Even with vote evidence, the SecretMafia substrate does not validate Village-side inference: informed Village seats gain 0.002 to 0.008 against a frozen baseline, inside noise. See cross_play_primary_evidence.

strict_boundaries: SCK never receives StoryBox backstage truth.
Evaluation may use truth only after decisions have been recorded.
Language generation may realize a CommunicationIntent but may not change the chosen strategic action.
StoryBox remains authoritative for legal actions and hard-world outcomes.
Behavioral evidence likelihood ratios must come from an explicit evidence model or replay calibration; the SecretMafia adapter does not hard-code social stereotypes.

benchmark_results.scope: 6 players, discussion_rounds=3, seeds 0-499 shared across all four variants, all seats driven by one policy
benchmark_results.direction_found: At 500 episodes action regret falls monotonically plain/memory 0.643 -> belief 0.541 -> belief_planning 0.492, village-side Brier is 0.0777 (belief) and 0.0772 (planning), leakage is zero everywhere, and the village faction win rate rises 0.146 -> 0.192 -> 0.304.
benchmark_results.attribution_problem: A belief-discrimination diagnostic (100 episodes, 1481 decisions) shows 74.1% of belief decisions had identical marginal probabilities across every legal target, and 100% for the Villager role. The belief therefore could not rank candidates and the tie-break alone picked the action. The measured improvement is reproducible but is not yet attributable to cognition, and the protect-regret gain is an artifact of the Doctor's and the Mafia's rules collapsing to the same 'lowest living id' tie-break.

vote_record_arm.what_it_is: A labelled sensitivity arm in which the runner reconstructs the day-vote record the environment broadcasts and then destroys, preserving submission order. Off by default; every view carrying it declares the channel and the information-safety audit enforces that.
vote_record_arm.channel_health: Belief-discrimination flat fraction falls from 0.741 to 0.465 overall, for the Villager role from 1.000 to 0.164, and in day voting from 0.504 to 0.086. The belief becomes a real inference engine.
vote_record_arm.play_outcome: Village faction win rate falls from 0.192 to 0.036 (belief) and from 0.304 to 0.068 (belief_planning), both far below the uniform-random baseline of 0.146, while regret barely moves (0.541 to 0.533).
vote_record_arm.conclusion: Action regret is not a valid proxy for playing well here, and the evidence model is mis-specified for play: recorded_vote_evidence only ever exonerates the player voted for, so the informed village avoids whoever is under suspicion, scatters its votes and never concentrates on a Mafia. The mechanism that should improve play makes it worse once it has data.
vote_record_arm.gate: MCTS, bi-level search and reconnecting SCK to the risk-list hospital Scene all remain held. SCK has no validated strategic improvement to offer StoryBox yet.

native_vote_channel.change: Target actions are now submitted as '[N]' instead of '[Player N]'. State.add_observation strips every '[Player N]' role tag from PLAYER_ACTION messages but leaves '[N]' alone, and the environment's own prompts ask for the '[X]' form.
native_vote_channel.controlled_evidence: Same policy and same seed: the two encodings produce identical roles, steps, termination reason and rewards, so the change affects observability only. With '[N]' zero PLAYER_ACTION observations arrive empty and 55 carry a real target; with '[Player N]' 55 arrive empty and zero carry a target.
native_vote_channel.conclusion: The native encoding fully replaces the reconstructed arm and needs no out-of-band repair, exactly as peer decision 0016 Q1 required. The reconstructed arm is retained only as a labelled sensitivity result for the legacy encoding, and the runner refuses to enable both at once because that would double-count the same evidence.

metric_status.renamed_per_peer_0016_Q5: mean_action_regret -> mean_immediate_target_loss_diagnostic, in storybox_sck_eval_v0.py and in the A/B harness, so no artifact implies true sequential regret.
metric_status.status: diagnostic only, never the acceptance metric
metric_status.reason: It scores immediate target correctness against a truth oracle and ignores downstream coordination, information value, tie mechanics and future responses. In the round 5 arm it improved while village play got three to five times worse. mafia_eliminate is additionally structurally non-discriminating because the Mafia's legal targets already exclude its own team.
metric_status.primary_metrics_now: paired cross-play terminal utility / faction win rate against fixed opponents, with calibration, discrimination flat fraction and leakage as mechanism gates

artifact_encoding_note: The 50-episode smoke test and both 500-episode artifacts were produced with the legacy '[Player N]' encoding. Plain and memory results are unchanged by the switch, but the belief variants' behaviour changes because they now receive vote evidence. Those artifacts are therefore retained as historical diagnostics only, per peer decision 0016 artifact_status_decision, and must not be compared against native-encoding runs.

cross_play_primary_evidence.design: 500 shared seeds per condition, 6 players, native [N] channel, arms assigned by role, frozen uniform-random baseline, zero information leakage
cross_play_primary_evidence.mechanism_finding: The Mafia gain is bloc voting, not inference. Informed Mafia seats vote unanimously at rate 1.000 against a 0.181 chance baseline, and that shared target is the plurality 96.3% of the time, while the four village seats scatter across about 2.6 distinct targets.
cross_play_primary_evidence.conclusion: The capability the gate exists to validate is hidden-information inference, which is the village side's task. Informed village seats gain 0.2 to 0.8 percentage points, indistinguishable from no effect at 500 episodes, while the mafia gain is a coordination artifact of two mirrored agents. Peer decision 0016 step 6 therefore applies: stop SecretMafia rule tuning and treat the substrate or feature model as insufficient for the intended high-skill claim.
cross_play_primary_evidence.methodological_gap: The frozen baseline is uniform random and cannot coordinate, so it is maximally exploitable by bloc voting and the mafia delta partly measures the baseline's weakness.

next_gate: continue from peer decision 2026-10-11-0021: SecretMafia tuning is stopped and the validation mainline moves to a mixed-motive peaceful repeated game

round 8: select one structured mixed-motive substrate, write its benchmark contract before running anything, and implement only the adapter and harness needed for a 20-50 episode smoke A/B across plain/memory/belief/belief_planning plus at least one fixed alternative policy

keep the SecretMafia artifacts as a retained adversarial negative benchmark: do not delete them, do not tune its rules, do not handcraft more evidence terms, and never claim strength from the mafia bloc gain

keep MCTS, bi-level search, the deferred meta-game/institutional-awareness runtime, the deferred Peak Play runtime and SCK-to-risk-list-hospital-Scene reconnection all held until the mixed-motive smoke gate shows a mechanism-attributable cognition gain

secretmafia_classification.main_claim: SCK v0 has not demonstrated improved hidden-information inference on SecretMafia Village play. The native channel, information-safety boundary and evaluation harness are valid enough to preserve this as a meaningful negative result.
secretmafia_classification.reusable_value: information-safety boundary pattern, native observation-channel validation method, cross-play harness, mechanism diagnostics, metric demotion

mixed_motive_substrate.why_own_authored: The TextArena survey found no usable third-party substrate that satisfies the peer contract. PublicGoodsGame and MarketEntryGame run but are fully symmetric, so they contain no hidden variable and the belief variants could not engage. BlindAuction has genuine private valuations but its reset raises TypeError in 0.7.4 because it constructs textarena.core.State with min_players/max_players/check_truncated, which that constructor does not accept. LetterAuction needs an NLTK corpus the sandbox blocks, and IteratedStagHunt needs numpy, which is not installed. An own-authored substrate is explicitly permitted but is weaker evidence than a third-party environment, and every result from it must carry that label.
